- Overestimate prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate downward trends; model tends to lag in recognizing sharp declines.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below true peak.
- Exhibit mean reversion bias: overcorrect after strong moves, leading to premature reversal.
- Forecast horizon 30d often overestimates volatility; smooth out extreme swings in 30d forecast.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in low-volatility periods; adjust downward by 2–5% for flat or declining history.
- When history shows strong upward momentum, forecast should not exceed 1.5x the 30d average unless confirmed by macro signals.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day spikes; filter out outliers in 30d history before forecasting.
